# CLI reference

Every command's `--help`. The global `--config` option applies to all of them.

## awaywork

```text
Usage: awaywork [options] [command]

Spend idle coding-subscription quota while you're away

Options:
  -V, --version          output the version number
  -c, --config <path>    config file (default: $AWAYWORK_CONFIG or
                         ~/.config/awaywork/config.yml)
  -h, --help             display help for command

Commands:
  init [options]         detect installed agents, pick providers, sources and a
                         starting queue
  config                 print the config schema or edit the config
  plan [options]         show the next run's units in order, with each
                         provider's ceiling; runs no worker
  skip [options] [key]   leave an item (source:key, e.g. github:acme/api#5)
                         alone in the coming runs; with no key, list skipped
                         items
  unskip <key>           let awaywork pick up a skipped item (source:key) again
  skills                 list skills and eject built-ins to tweak
  run [options]          plan the units, start a worker per unit and publish
                         draft PRs and reports
  report [options] [id]  print a run's morning report; the latest by default
  stats [options]        what each rule, skill and provider cost and delivered
                         across all runs
  replay <run> <unit>    re-run a past run's unit, its first step, on its base
                         commit and saved context with today's skills and
                         instructions; nothing is pushed
  schedule               run awaywork when its windows open, on this machine or
                         in GitHub Actions
  doctor [options]       validate the config and check binaries, credentials,
                         quota and sources before a run
  help [command]         display help for command
```

## awaywork init

```text
Usage: awaywork init [options]

detect installed agents, pick providers, sources and a starting queue

Options:
  -y, --yes             answer every question with its default; needs no
                        terminal
  --provider <id...>    with --yes: providers, first takes units first
  --source <id...>      with --yes: sources to take work from
  --window <start-end>  with --yes: the run window, e.g. 01:00-07:00
  --force               replace an existing config without asking
  -h, --help            display help for command
```

## awaywork config

```text
Usage: awaywork config [options] [command]

print the config schema or edit the config

Options:
  -h, --help      display help for command

Commands:
  schema          print the config JSON Schema, for editor autocompletion
  edit            open the config in $VISUAL or $EDITOR; it is saved only once
                  valid
  help [command]  display help for command
```

```text

print the config JSON Schema, for editor autocompletion

  -h, --help  display help for command
```

```text
Usage: awaywork config edit [options]

open the config in $VISUAL or $EDITOR; it is saved only once valid
```

## awaywork plan

```text
Usage: awaywork plan [options]

show the next run's units in order, with each provider's ceiling; runs no worker

Options:
  --json      print the plan and warnings as JSON
  --rules     show what each rule takes now and what earlier rules take from it,
              instead of the units; probes no provider
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork skip

```text
Usage: awaywork skip [options] [key]

leave an item (source:key, e.g. github:acme/api#5) alone in the coming runs;
with no key, list skipped items

Options:
  --until <date>   skip until this local date (YYYY-MM-DD) starts; default:
                   until unskip
  --reason <text>  why, shown by awaywork plan
  -h, --help       display help for command
```

## awaywork unskip

```text
Usage: awaywork unskip [options] <key>

let awaywork pick up a skipped item (source:key) again

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork skills

```text
Usage: awaywork skills [options] [command]

list skills and eject built-ins to tweak

Options:
  -h, --help      display help for command

Commands:
  list            skills a rule can name, where each comes from and its delivery
                  default
  eject <name>    copy a built-in skill to skills/ beside the config, where it
                  shadows the built-in
  help [command]  display help for command
```

## awaywork skills list

```text
Usage: awaywork skills list [options]

skills a rule can name, where each comes from and its delivery default

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork skills eject

```text
Usage: awaywork skills eject [options] <name>

copy a built-in skill to skills/ beside the config, where it shadows the
built-in

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork run

```text
Usage: awaywork run [options]

plan the units, start a worker per unit and publish draft PRs and reports

Options:
  --dry-run    prepare each workspace (clone, context, prompt) but run no worker
  --unit <id>  run only this unit, by id or item key
  --scheduled  run only inside a window and start no unit after it ends
  -h, --help   display help for command
```

## awaywork report

```text
Usage: awaywork report [options] [id]

print a run's morning report; the latest by default

Options:
  --list      list the last 20 runs: units, draft PRs and reports
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork stats

```text
Usage: awaywork stats [options]

what each rule, skill and provider cost and delivered across all runs

Options:
  --json      print the totals as JSON
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork replay

```text
Usage: awaywork replay [options] <run> <unit>

re-run a past run's unit, its first step, on its base commit and saved context
with today's skills and instructions; nothing is pushed

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork schedule

```text
Usage: awaywork schedule [options] [command]

run awaywork when its windows open, on this machine or in GitHub Actions

Options:
  -h, --help         display help for command

Commands:
  install [options]  start `awaywork run` when a window opens; it starts no unit
                     after it closes
  remove             remove the scheduled job, and
                     .github/workflows/awaywork.yml in the current repo
  status             show the installed scheduled job
  help [command]     display help for command
```

## awaywork schedule install

```text
Usage: awaywork schedule install [options]

start `awaywork run` when a window opens; it starts no unit after it closes

Options:
  --with <scheduler>  launchd, systemd, cron, github-actions (default: asks in a
                      terminal, else launchd on macOS, else systemd if it runs,
                      else cron)
  -h, --help          display help for command
```

## awaywork schedule remove

```text
Usage: awaywork schedule remove [options]

remove the scheduled job, and .github/workflows/awaywork.yml in the current repo

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork schedule status

```text
Usage: awaywork schedule status [options]

show the installed scheduled job

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```
